subject: Tenant locality + configurable retention by legal jurisdiction - requirements & timeline
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@finapps.co>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant locality & retention by legal jurisdiction - quickQ

Hi Vanessa,

Quick question from our legal/data-privacy team: we have customers in the EU and LATAM who require that customer data be stored and deleted per their local laws. Can Redwood support per-tenant retention policies that are bound to a legal jurisdiction (e.g., EU GDPR 6-month retention for certain PII, APAC retention exceptions), and ensure physical storage locality so data never leaves the chosen region? Also: what are the controls around legal holds (ability to suspend deletion) and audit logs for erase events?

We'd like a short list of what is possible today, what requires roadmap work, and a rough timeline — our procurement deadline is the end of Q4.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Legal Ops, FinApps

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Tenant locality & retention by legal jurisdiction - quickQ

Thanks Alicia — good questions. High level answers below, and I want to get engineering + product in the loop to confirm technical constraints and a realistic delivery window.

Summary (short):
- Today: regional storage routing exists at region-level for hosted tenants (region selection on workspace creation) but retention is global and not tenant-scoped.
- Roadmap work needed: per-tenant TTLs, per-tenant region pinning for object-store + KV cache, and erasure workflow that is jurisdiction-aware.
- Legal hold: can be implemented as a suspend-delete flag but we need to validate cross-region hold semantics.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync this week to capture FinApps requirements and confirm non-negotiables? I attached a short template to capture retention buckets and legal-hold policies if you want to pre-fill.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Thanks for looping us in. A couple of engineering notes to frame the sync:

- Storage locality: we can pin blobs/objects to a single region at workspace creation and avoid cross-region replication, provided the customer does not enable cross-region backups. That is feasible today for dedicated/private but we need UI/console and API surface for hosted workspaces.
- TTL per-tenant: two pieces — metadata-level TTL (index/manifest) and blob-level garbage collection. Implementing tenant-scoped TTLs requires changes in: the router (to tag objects with tenant_jurisdiction), the lifecycle worker (to honor jurisdiction-aware TTLs), and the deletion pipeline (to build replayable erase jobs).
- KV cache / ephemeral state: we currently have per-node caches; KV eviction doesn't tie to tenant TTLs. For strict erasure guarantees we'd need cache invalidation hooks and a short-lived KV epoch for tenants with stricter erase windows.
- Legal hold: legal holds are primarily an orchestration concern (suspend deletion) but also affect retention billing and audit records — we must ensure freeze markers are stored in the same region as the subject data to avoid cross-border dependencies.

Effort estimate (very rough):
- Minimal viable: API + console flag to select "region-locked storage" + tenant TTL index change + admin erase job orchestration: ~2-3 sprints (6 weeks) from prioritization.
- Full compliance offering (audit-grade erase logs, legal-hold UI, cross-region guardrails, SLA language): 3-4 quarters.

I'll add a short tech note to the sync. We need FinApps to confirm: 1) whether legal holds are expected to stop all forms of deletion (including snapshots/backups), and 2) whether KMS keys must be region-restricted.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Sep 2028 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant locality & retention by legal jurisdiction - quickQ

Couple of compliance points to capture before the sync with FinApps: 

- Legal hold scope: confirm whether legal holds must apply to exportable artifacts (logs, debug traces) and third-party backups. If yes, we need to extend hold markers into our backup orchestration and partner snapshots (this will add complexity and likely push to the longer timeline).
- KMS: most customers expect a KMS-per-region model. If FinApps requires a customer-managed key (CMK) or HSM in-region, that becomes an enterprise-only offering unless we expand hosted key options.
- Audit logs: retention and immutability expectations differ by jurisdiction; our audit export pipelines must be able to target region-specific logging endpoints.

I'll prepare a compliance checklist for the meeting.

—Irene
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference

Alicia — thanks, team and FinApps for the quick replies. Per our conversation I pulled together a mutual action plan (MAP) so we have clear decision points. Please review and confirm; I've attached a short proposal we will use to track the MVP scope.

Mutual Action Plan (MVP scope):
1) Confirm per-tenant jurisdiction mapping (FinApps to provide mapping file) — due 2028-09-11
2) Decide on legal-hold semantics (suspend deletions only vs suspend + quarantine backups) — due 2028-09-18
3) Prioritize region-locked storage for hosted workspaces (engineering to scope API/console changes) — Redwood to commit a tentative 6-week ETA for the MVP after requirements sign-off
4) Agree KMS approach (Redwood-managed per-region vs customer-managed KMS enterprise add-on) — due 2028-09-25

Attachments: MVP-retention-proposal-v1.pdf (short scope doc), finapps-data-requirements-20280904.xlsx (template for jurisdiction mapping).

Best,
